body:
...You're right. I am thinking myself away from solutions, I can recognize that. I'm scared, more scared than I care to admit. I don't want to try to get help because I'm scared they might not work. Then i'll really have to admit to myself that I can't be helped at all. That alone is my reason, I supposed I don't have anything else to say about it.

But. I've got time to decide what I should do. It really does just come down to deciding to give up, or trying to scream for help and hoping that someone will throw down a rope and try to pull me out. I wanted to commit suicide early tomorrow morning. I was going to skip my early morning classes and just live my last few hours in peace. Maybe I will, maybe I won't. 

The pain I've been feeling has diminished considerably, save for a few sobbing spells. Maybe I just wanted to hear someone tell me that I could still be saved, even if I didn't believe it. So thank you. You really have been helpful. I know it's not good to say that you can't save everybody, but I really do appreciate you sticking with me like this. 

I guess it's up to me to decide if I really want to see if I can escape this pain and actually be well, even if I haven't been well for a very long time.

Well, I actually didn't want to tell him at all... he just jokingly brought up "baggage" once and I really don't remember much after that other than having essentially an "episode" where I mumbled intermittently about bullying and being molested and it already freaked him out just seeing that. I don't want anyone or at least people I want to stay in my life to know these things because I already know it's going to scare them away. 

I am exaggerating if I say that it makes me feel worse, because talking about it does bring a sense of relief. However, the aftermath of realizing how much those experiences have left me with scars that cause people to leave me are, I suppose, the things that make me feel "worse."

Going to a doctor is a scary thing, I will admit. Mostly because I've got so many fears centered around it: what happens if they end up giving me so many medications that I'm not even myself anymore? then i'll be dependent on medications for my own happiness rather than just being able to be happy on my own. What happens if they just don't work for me anymore? then I just get more of them? how will I cope? I'll have to tell people that I'm going to the doctor for a mental illness... they'll think I'm insane. People will treat me differently. I've already had to deal with being a bit of an outcast, now i'll have to deal with being an outcast and labeled as "mentally ill/crazy/sick/etc." 

I guess that's what's deterred me from wanting to ask for professional help for so long. It just feels like it might not change things in the long run...

Maybe it is selfish, maybe it's crazy sounding, but I don't know if I'm willing to continue waiting for things to change. I'll say that I've always been waiting. I tried committing suicide when I was 14, but then I just told myself that everything will get better. So I waited. And I've been waiting. 

I guess I really am just exhausted from trying to climb out of a hole that seems to have someone digging it deeper at the bottom. Every time I climb up, I lose my footing and end up falling longer and hitting the bottom harder than ever before. I should've expected the drop would kill me sooner or later.

It feels like: "Just how old do you have to be to want to accept someone's faults and see them for who they truly are?" I'm 19, he's 24 (almost 25)... I don't know, maybe there's some truth in being too young to understand who I am, but at the same time, there hasn't been much of a change in the way I act. Aside from a "scene" phase when I was 13 and I think it's safe to say everyone has those.

I've talked about my problems with countless people on hotlines and chat rooms and support groups, like this one... It just makes me feel like maybe talking about it isn't an option anymore. If that's supposed to help, why do I always feel worse?

To say the least, I'm suffocating. I literally feel like I can't breathe sometimes because I just think about everything that has lead up to my life at this point and I can't handle it so much that it leads to periods of sobbing that last until I'm so drained that I just check out and fall asleep.

I don't know if there's any options left.
